Gyo.name: Gyo
Gyo.description: Focus aura into the eyes to perceive hidden auras and In-concealed Nen constructs with crystal clarity. A fundamental perception technique requiring minimal aura expenditure (roughly 2-3% per use), essential for reading an opponent's true strength and detecting assassins or cloaked threats.

Shu.name: Shu
Shu.description: Extend one's aura over a held object to enhance its durability, sensitivity, or striking power. Requires sustained concentration (3-5% aura drain per turn) and allows fine control over enhancement intensity, making it indispensable for weapon users and tactical support specialists.

In.name: In
In.description: Conceal one's own Nen constructs and aura emissions, rendering them invisible to Gyo and normal perception. The concealment consumes minimal aura to maintain but demands perfect control; detection risks exposing the user's position or technique.

Ken.name: Ken
Ken.description: Coat the entire body in a sustained Ren guard, distributing aura evenly across all limbs and torso for comprehensive defense. Drains 3-5% aura per turn while active but significantly reduces all incoming damage; essential for protracted battles and defensive specialists.

Ko.name: Ko
Ko.description: Concentrate all available aura into a single point for a devastating, unstoppable strike that pierces through defenses. Costs 25-40% of maximum aura in one explosive burst; leaves the user defenseless elsewhere and requires perfect timing to be effective.

Ryu.name: Ryu
Ryu.description: Achieve real-time flow control between Ko and Ken states, seamlessly shifting aura focus from defensive coverage to concentrated strikes mid-combat. A master technique that demands extreme precision and costs 5-10% aura per shift; grants unmatched tactical flexibility to elite practitioners.

En.name: En
En.description: Project a spherical aura field outward to sense all living beings and Nen constructs within its radius with perfect clarity. One of Nen's most demanding techniques, draining 10%+ aura per turn and accessible only to Masters who have transcended category limitations; the sheer power draws immediate attention.

En (Prodigy).name: En (Prodigy)
En (Prodigy).description: Project a spherical aura field outward to sense all living beings and Nen constructs within its radius with perfect clarity. An accelerated mastery path for gifted Enhancers, allowing En activation at an earlier stage through raw aura capacity and tactical acumen; maintains the same drain and sensory effect as the Master version.

En (Aberrant).name: En (Aberrant)
En (Aberrant).description: Project a spherical aura field outward to sense all living beings and Nen constructs within its radius with perfect clarity. A rare deviation from canon mastery, available to Specialists whose anomalous nature grants them early access; provides identical sensing capability despite flowing from fundamentally different Nen principles.

Nascent Hatsu (Enhancement).name: Nascent Hatsu (Enhancement)
Nascent Hatsu (Enhancement).description: This is your personal Nen technique in embryo—a unique power waiting to bloom through blood, sweat, and discovery. The narrator will help you name it, define its form, and grow it through play; Enhancement Hatsu strengthen bodies and objects, turning flesh into steel and steel into lightning.

Nascent Hatsu (Transmutation).name: Nascent Hatsu (Transmutation)
Nascent Hatsu (Transmutation).description: This is your personal Nen technique in embryo—a unique power waiting to bloom through blood, sweat, and discovery. The narrator will help you name it, define its form, and grow it through play; Transmutation Hatsu reshape aura into the properties of other substances—water, electricity, oil, shadow.

Nascent Hatsu (Conjuration).name: Nascent Hatsu (Conjuration)
Nascent Hatsu (Conjuration).description: This is your personal Nen technique in embryo—a unique power waiting to bloom through blood, sweat, and discovery. The narrator will help you name it, define its form, and grow it through play; Conjuration Hatsu materialize objects from nothing—weapons, armor, tools—each bound by rules that define its nature.

Nascent Hatsu (Emission).name: Nascent Hatsu (Emission)
Nascent Hatsu (Emission).description: This is your personal Nen technique in embryo—a unique power waiting to bloom through blood, sweat, and discovery. The narrator will help you name it, define its form, and grow it through play; Emission Hatsu release aura independent of the body—projectiles, blasts, conjured familiars sent forth to act.

Nascent Hatsu (Manipulation).name: Nascent Hatsu (Manipulation)
Nascent Hatsu (Manipulation).description: This is your personal Nen technique in embryo—a unique power waiting to bloom through blood, sweat, and discovery. The narrator will help you name it, define its form, and grow it through play; Manipulation Hatsu control objects and beings through a medium—threads, chains, puppets—extending your will through the world.

Nascent Hatsu (Specialization).name: Nascent Hatsu (Specialization)
Nascent Hatsu (Specialization).description: This is your personal Nen technique in embryo—a unique power waiting to bloom through blood, sweat, and discovery. The narrator will help you name it, define its form, and grow it through play; Specialization Hatsu bend Nen's rules in unique ways—vows that grant power, conditions that reshape reality, anomalies that defy categorization.

Jajanken: Rock.name: Jajanken: Rock
Jajanken: Rock.description: Gon's most devastating technique—a fully charged fist strike enhanced with total aura concentration. The mandatory chant is a binding vow that channels his entire Enhancement prowess into a single, unstoppable blow. Consumes 35-40% aura in one catastrophic impact and requires a full turn to charge; known for piercing through all defenses.

Jajanken: Scissors.name: Jajanken: Scissors
Jajanken: Scissors.description: An aura blade formed between Gon's fingers, extended mid-range with sharp, cutting efficiency. Costs 12-18% aura and allows quick slashing strikes or mid-combat repositioning. Less devastating than Rock but far more flexible, enabling rapid offensive and evasive maneuvers.

Jajanken: Paper.name: Jajanken: Paper
Jajanken: Paper.description: Gon launches a flat, emitted wave of concentrated aura that travels outward as an expanding projectile. Costs 12-18% aura and provides ranged suppression, area denial, or defensive coverage. Weaker individually than Rock or Scissors but enables flexibility in spacing and crowd control.

Lightning Palm.name: Lightning Palm
Lightning Palm.description: Killua discharges electrical aura through his grip, supercharging a melee contact into a paralytic shock. Costs 8-12% aura per strike and can be applied to grapples, throws, or close-quarters holds for devastating effect. The electrical charge lingers briefly on contact, potentially spreading to nearby targets.

Thunderbolt.name: Thunderbolt
Thunderbolt.description: Killua releases a lance of electrical aura from his fingertips, striking with speed and precision over mid-range. Costs 15-20% aura per shot and allows rapid-fire volleys or precise targeting. The lightning arcs slightly, making it difficult to predict the final impact point.

Godspeed.name: Godspeed
Godspeed.description: Killua's ultimate technique—a whirlwind of electricity that grants both automatic defensive reactions and willed hyperspeed movement. Combines Whirlwind's passive evasion with Speed of Lightning's devastating mobility, but drains 25-40% aura per turn while active. The sustained output is catastrophic; only Masters can maintain it long-term. Requires advanced Transmutation mastery and kills all other auras nearby.

Holy Chain.name: Holy Chain
Holy Chain.description: Kurapika conjures a thin golden chain from his thumb, capable of borrowing the enhancement aura of allies to facilitate healing or restoration. Costs 10-15% aura to activate and serves as both utility support and medium for Enhancement-based recovery. The chain dissolves if broken and must be recharged to reform.

Chain Jail.name: Chain Jail
Chain Jail.description: Kurapika conjures a thick middle-finger chain that wraps around and binds an opponent, forcing them into Zetsu (complete aura shutdown). Costs 18-25% aura and requires the target to be restrained; once activated, the bound target cannot access Nen. WARNING: This ability only works on members of the Phantom Troupe due to an ancient Kurta clan vow—using it on anyone else triggers an automatic death curse.

Dowsing Chain.name: Dowsing Chain
Dowsing Chain.description: Kurapika manifests a chain with a spinning ball attached, which gravitates toward objects or people based on Kurapika's will. Costs 8-12% aura and serves as a truth-detection tool and tracking device; the chain cannot lie about what it finds. Useful for locating targets and verifying truthfulness in interrogations.

Judgment Chain.name: Judgment Chain
Judgment Chain.description: Kurapika's most fearsome ability—a chain conjured from the little finger that transforms into a razor-sharp blade capable of inscribing two binding conditions on a target. Costs 20-30% aura; the conditions are permanent and enforced by the chain itself—violation of either condition stops the target's heart instantly. The narrator must strictly enforce the stated conditions.

Emperor Time.name: Emperor Time
Emperor Time.description: Kurapika's Scarlet Eyes ascend into absolute Nen efficiency—100% mastery across all Nen categories simultaneously. Costs 1 hour of lifespan per second of use. The narrator enforces this merciless price mechanically; continued use visibly ages Kurapika and threatens permanent death. All aura expenditures are optimized; no waste occurs. An ability that trades mortality for omnipotence.

Remote Punch.name: Remote Punch
Remote Punch.description: Leorio conjures a warp-portal haymaker that travels through space, striking from unexpected angles and distances. Costs 15-20% aura per punch and allows targeting of distant or obscured enemies. The portal effect prevents interception mid-flight; the impact lands with full force regardless of distance.

Bungee Gum.name: Bungee Gum
Bungee Gum.description: Hisoka's signature technique—manifests elastic aura with the dual properties of rubber and gum. Costs 15-20% aura and enables versatile attachment/retraction mechanics for attack, defense, traversal, or trapping. The gum-like adhesion is nearly impossible to break; the rubber elasticity grants enormous flexibility in application and rebound.

Texture Surprise.name: Texture Surprise
Texture Surprise.description: Hisoka forges aura-skin over his own body to assume convincing false appearances or tactile mimicry. Costs 8-12% aura per transformation and serves as deception utility for infiltration, interrogation misdirection, or psychological warfare. The illusion is detailed enough to fool casual observation but may fail under intense scrutiny.

Needle People.name: Needle People
Needle People.description: Illumi conjures hair-thin needles that pierce flesh and enslave the nervous system or reshape physical form entirely. Costs 15-25% aura per insertion and allows both offensive domination (controlling a host) and modification (altering appearance, implanting suggestions). The host can serve as a living puppet or undergo permanent physical transformation.

Skill Hunter.name: Skill Hunter
Skill Hunter.description: Chrollo's foundational ability—casts stolen Hatsu abilities directly from the Bandit's Secret, a conjured book that must remain open and held in hand. Costs 10-15% aura per ability cast and grants perfect execution of any stolen technique. The book is a binding limitation; closing or losing it ends all active stolen abilities instantly.

Steal the Ability.name: Steal the Ability
Steal the Ability.description: Chrollo permanently steals a single Hatsu ability from an opponent through a four-step ritual: witness the technique in use, ask the target about it directly, receive their answer (they must respond truthfully or willfully ignore), and perform palm-to-palm contact to complete the theft. Costs 20-30% aura for the transfer. This is a narrative heist tool with strict conditions—all four steps must occur within one hour and the target must survive the encounter for the theft to take permanent hold.

Battōjutsu: Severing Circle.name: Battōjutsu: Severing Circle
Battōjutsu: Severing Circle.description: Nobunaga draws his sword with blinding iaido speed, severing anything within a 4-meter radius of his En simultaneously. Costs 18-25% aura and requires precise distance management to be effective. The cutting arc occurs in an instant; targets caught within his En range cannot escape the strike.

Pain Packer: Rising Sun.name: Pain Packer: Rising Sun
Pain Packer: Rising Sun.description: Feitan transforms accumulated pain into a miniature sun that explodes outward with devastating radiance. Costs 25-40% aura and scales in power based on accumulated damage to Feitan before use—greater pain yields greater output. The sun's armor punishes nearby combatants with heat damage; the technique is as much punishment for opponents as it is cathartic release for Feitan.

Nen Stitches.name: Nen Stitches
Nen Stitches.description: Machi manifests aura-threads from her fingertips, capable of sewing flesh together, tracking movement via airborne strands, or garroting targets from distance. Costs 10-15% aura per stitch-application and allows sustained control of threads across a wide area. The threads are nearly invisible and difficult to cut without specialized techniques.

Ripper Cyclotron.name: Ripper Cyclotron
Ripper Cyclotron.description: Phinks winds his aura tighter with each rotation, building exponential power that culminates in a devastating spin strike. Costs 15-25% aura and scales unpredictably based on winding speed—the number of rotations must be called before execution, but precise metering is difficult in combat. More winds equal more power, but also more time and commitment required.

Double Machine Gun.name: Double Machine Gun
Double Machine Gun.description: Franklin emits torrents of aura bullets from his fingertips with machine-gun rapidity. Costs 15-20% aura per volley and allows sustained fire across wide areas, excellent for area denial and suppressive tactics. The bullets lack piercing power individually but overwhelm through sheer volume.

Black Voice.name: Black Voice
Black Voice.description: Shalnark implants an antenna into a target's body, granting him absolute control over their actions and perceptions. Costs 18-25% aura to implant and allows sustained puppet-mastery of the victim. WARNING: If Shalnark uses Black Voice on himself via 'Autopilot,' he becomes a blind, paralyzed passenger while his body acts autonomously—a terrible cost paid for unthinking combat efficiency.

Blinky.name: Blinky
Blinky.description: Shizuku conjures a sentient vacuum that consumes anything Shizuku declares trash. Costs 12-18% aura per activation and functions as a traversal/storage/trap mechanism. The vacuum never consumes living creatures or Nen constructs that Shizuku consciously remembers; target selection is entirely subjective to Shizuku's definition of 'trash.'

Memory Bomb.name: Memory Bomb
Memory Bomb.description: Pakunoda touches an object or person to psychometrically read all associated memories, then fires those memories into another target's mind as a disorienting psychological assault. Costs 18-25% aura and serves as both intelligence-gathering tool and combat utility. The implanted memories overwhelm the target's senses; execution can be devastating or merely incapacitating.

Big Bang Impact.name: Big Bang Impact
Big Bang Impact.description: Uvogin's signature finishing move—an aura-enhanced physical blow of unparalleled crushing force. Costs 25-40% aura and requires full body commitment; the impact creates a localized shockwave that devastates everything in its path. The Spider's heaviest physical strike, reserved for finishing opponents or breaking through major obstacles.

Battle Cantabile: Jupiter.name: Battle Cantabile: Jupiter
Battle Cantabile: Jupiter.description: Bonolenov performs a martial dance accompanied by conjured music that materializes planetary mass at his position. Costs 18-25% aura per musical phrase and requires continuous movement/chanting to maintain. The conjured planet-scale force provides overwhelming area denial and devastating collision damage; the technique grows more powerful the longer the performance continues.

Gallery Fake.name: Gallery Fake
Gallery Fake.description: Kortopi conjures perfect 24-hour copies of any object he has touched. Costs 15-20% aura per copy and allows sustained creation of duplicates for infiltration, misdirection, or substitution tactics. The copies remain linked to Kortopi's awareness; he can sense through them and track their locations indefinitely.

Dance of the Serpent's Bite.name: Dance of the Serpent's Bite
Dance of the Serpent's Bite.description: Kalluto wields paper fans infused with aura, layering them with confetti misdirection to create visual chaos and slicing attacks. Costs 12-18% aura per maneuver and allows rapid repositioning and target confusion through layered fan strikes and scattered aura-paper. The confetti cloud obscures sight and tracking; precision targeting becomes nearly impossible.

requirements.variable: Hatsu: Dance of the Serpent's Bite

Dragon Lance.name: Dragon Lance
Dragon Lance.description: Zeno conjures an enormous aura dragon that pierces through opposition with devastating penetrating force. Costs 20-30% aura and serves as both direct assault and immovable object; the dragon's trajectory is precise and difficult to evade. A variant form, Dragon Dive, sacrifices penetration for impact force, creating massive area damage on collision.

Twin Orbs.name: Twin Orbs
Twin Orbs.description: Silva manifests twin spheres of compressed aura, each humming with lethal potential. Costs 18-25% aura per sphere and allows independent targeting or synchronized detonation. The orbs carry the weight of Silva's raw enhancement power, capable of piercing through heavy fortifications and Nen armor with brutal efficiency.

Nanika's Wish.name: Nanika's Wish
Nanika's Wish.description: Killua's parasitic sister grants any wish after three prior requests have been fulfilled. The price scales precisely to the wish's magnitude—greater wishes demand greater costs, often lives or years of life. Failure to pay the price accrues as a debt that compounds with interest. EXCEPTION: Killua holds unique command authority and may issue orders directly without request-fulfillment. The narrator must mechanically enforce all payment terms and track accumulated debt.

Coin Bullets.name: Coin Bullets
Coin Bullets.description: Gotoh flicks ordinary coins with surgical precision, accelerating them to gunfire velocity and beyond. Costs 8-12% aura per shot and allows rapid, unpredictable fire from concealment. The coins are nearly impossible to trace; their small profile and high speed make them ideal for assassination or precision elimination.

Rider's High.name: Rider's High
Rider's High.description: Tsubone transforms her body into any wheeled or tracked vehicle, becoming a living conveyance. Costs 15-20% aura per transformation and allows others to ride/fuel her through Nen transfer. The transformed state grants mobility appropriate to the vehicle type; different forms enable different tactical roles.

100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva.name: 100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva
100-Type Guanyin Bodhisattva.description: Netero's prayer-born goddess materializes as a colossal Nen avatar channeling his accumulated devotion. The technique escalates through ninety-nine hand techniques, each amplifying power exponentially—First Hand through Ninety-Ninth Hand to the absolute Zero Hand, which expends every drop of Netero's aura for an all-encompassing, reality-bending strike. Costs 25-50% per hand escalation; Zero Hand leaves him completely empty. The narrator must strictly enforce the cost and escalation sequence.

Cattle Bell.name: Cattle Bell
Cattle Bell.description: Mizaistom conjures judgment cards that impose restraints or render binding verdicts on targets. Costs 10-15% aura per card and serves as conditional control—the targeted entity faces the stated judgment. Useful for negotiation, enforcement, and strategic incapacitation of dangerous combatants.

Three Monkeys.name: Three Monkeys
Three Monkeys.description: Saiyu's staff strikes impose psychic prisons that blind, deafen, or silence targets—the three monkey conditions. Costs 12-18% aura per strike and requires staff contact to activate. A target bound by See-Not cannot track visually, one bound by Hear-Not cannot receive audio signals, and one bound by Speak-Not cannot vocalize or cast voice-based Nen techniques. The narrator enforces these sensory deprivations strictly.

Technique Mimicry.name: Technique Mimicry
Technique Mimicry.description: Ging replicates any Nen technique he has personally received or witnessed in direct combat. Costs 15-25% aura per replication and allows perfect execution matching the original user's proficiency. Limited to techniques he has directly experienced; merely hearing about an ability does not grant replication rights.

Tiger Bite Double.name: Tiger Bite Double
Tiger Bite Double.description: Kastro conjures a perfect doppelgänger of himself, doubling his combat presence and striking capability. Costs 20-30% aura to maintain the double and drains additional aura if the double takes damage. CRITICAL FLAW: Controlling the double causes severe memory-overdraft effects in Kastro's mind—sustained use risks cognitive degradation and personality fragmentation.

Song of Healing.name: Song of Healing
Song of Healing.description: Melody plays a soothing flute melody that calms minds and bodies, restoring vitality to allies within earshot. Costs 8-12% aura per performance and serves as utility support—accelerates healing, steadies panicked allies, and relieves psychological distress. The melody must remain uninterrupted; broken concentration cancels the effect.

Great Haiku.name: Great Haiku
Great Haiku.description: Basho declares a verse in the traditional 5-7-5 syllable structure, and the declared poem becomes reality in proportion to its literary quality and emotional resonance. Costs 12-18% aura per haiku and serves as conditional reality-alteration—a perfectly crafted verse manifests more completely than a clumsy one. The narrator judges the haiku's artistic merit to determine effect magnitude.

Lovely Ghostwriter.name: Lovely Ghostwriter
Lovely Ghostwriter.description: Neon's automatic-writing prophecy manifests cryptic, poetic verses that reveal potential futures and hidden truths. Costs 18-25% aura per prophecy session and produces information involuntarily—Neon cannot consciously control or read her own output, making interpretation a collaborative process. The prophecies are always accurate but deliberately obscure, requiring narrative decoding.

Magical Esthetician.name: Magical Esthetician
Magical Esthetician.description: Bisky summons Cookie-chan, a conjured esthetician companion who performs massage and restoration magic. Costs 12-18% aura per session and grants 30 minutes of uninterrupted treatment equivalent to 8 hours of natural sleep, erasing fatigue and mental strain completely. The conjured esthetician cannot engage in combat but provides invaluable recovery support.

14 Devils.name: 14 Devils
14 Devils.description: Razor emits a gang of fourteen powerful demon constructs, each with independent agency and distinct capabilities. Costs 25-35% aura for full summoning and allows sustained control of the squad. The demons operate under strict rules—they acknowledge the Nen dodgeball court ruleset and respect those boundaries. Each demon can be dismissed individually to conserve aura.

Little Flower.name: Little Flower
Little Flower.description: A palm-contact explosion that detonates on impact, releasing devastating concussive force. Costs 10-15% aura per detonation and serves as a close-range offensive tool. The technique is simple but extremely effective at destroying fortifications and overpowering direct opposition.

Countdown.name: Countdown
Countdown.description: Plant a time-bomb Nen construct that detonates on a specified delay or trigger condition. Costs 18-25% aura per bomb placement and allows strategic trapping. Release conditions are strict: only the planter can trigger early release; defusal requires severing the Nen connection or equivalent magical nullification. The narrator mechanically enforces all timer mechanics.

Twin Gorillas.name: Twin Gorillas
Twin Gorillas.description: White conjures two massive gorilla constructs, enabling rapid positional swaps. Costs 15-20% aura and allows White to swap positions with one gorilla, and the gorillas to swap with targets within their range. The technique enables hit-and-run tactics and chaotic spatial manipulation.

Exorcist's Beast.name: Exorcist's Beast
Exorcist's Beast.description: Summon a parasitic-eating entity through a binding ritual, consuming foreign Nen constructs and aura-based afflictions from a target. Costs 20-30% aura per ritual invocation and serves as specialized utility for removing curses, unwanted Nen attachments, or contaminated aura. CRITICAL: Each exorcism requires binding ritual preparation; the process cannot be rushed or improvised.

Crazy Slots.name: Crazy Slots
Crazy Slots.description: Roll a slot machine that conjures a random weapon numbered 1-9—a gun, sword, spear, shuriken, or others. Costs 10-15% aura per roll and binds the user to the result until the weapon is used or discarded. No re-rolls are permitted until deployment; inability to choose is a binding limitation. The clown attendant talks back, offering cryptic commentary on each roll. (A hidden tenth outcome may exist, but remains mysterious.)

Deep Purple.name: Deep Purple
Deep Purple.description: Morel transforms his pipe-breath into sentient smoke constructs capable of independent action within a defined radius. Costs 20-30% aura per summon and creates an entire subordinate army bound by Morel's breath capacity—the larger his aura reserve, the more constructs he can sustain. The smoke cloud obscures vision and allows mobile fortification.

Hide and Seek.name: Hide and Seek
Hide and Seek.description: Knov manifests pocket-dimension apartments accessible through Nen-infused windows and exits. Costs 15-25% aura per portal creation and grants interior space independent of exterior reality. The 4th floor is permanently restricted and cannot be accessed by normal means; traversal to restricted zones requires explicit narrative permission.

Hakoware.name: Hakoware
Hakoware.description: Knuckle lends Nen power as debt through his A.P.R. system, charging exponential interest compounded interest on borrowed aura. Costs 0 aura to lend (debt-based), but failure to repay interest accrues bankruptcy penalties—forced Zetsu for 30 consecutive days. The I.R.S. enforcement rules are strict and narrator-enforced; debt cannot be escaped through death or incapacitation.

Hotel Rafflesia.name: Hotel Rafflesia
Hotel Rafflesia.description: Shoot manifests three independent floating hands capable of manipulation and construction, encaging targets within an expanding birdcage barrier. Costs 18-25% aura per construct and allows defensive fortification or offensive encirclement. CRITICAL: Targets within the birdcage are subject to continuous shrinking—the longer they remain trapped, the smaller they become, eventually becoming insignificant.

Wink Blue.name: Wink Blue
Wink Blue.description: Palm's third eye grants clairvoyant vision of anyone she has previously beheld directly. Costs 8-12% aura to activate and provides real-time visual contact with distant targets. Once a person enters the third eye's memory, they can never hide from Palm's perception.

Terpsichora.name: Terpsichora
Terpsichora.description: Neferpitou achieves supreme marionette mastery, puppeting defeated opponents as perfect extensions of will while granting surgical precision through conjured Doctor Blythe field medicine. Costs 25-40% aura per marionette and allows full cognitive control of puppet-bodies. Doctor Blythe procedures can be performed mid-combat, healing or modifying puppets as needed. The narrator enforces all puppet limitations and surgical precision rules.

Future Sight.name: Future Sight
Future Sight.description: Tserriednich perceives ten seconds of potential future while holding his breath, gaining precognitive advantage in decision-making and combat. Costs 8-12% aura per use and requires continuous breath-holding to maintain; release of breath ends the vision immediately. SPECULATIVE: This ability extends beyond manga canon and should be treated as an extrapolated interpretation—the narrator may adjust mechanics or range as narrative appropriateness demands.

death.instructions: In this world, no one walks away from death clean. When a character falls, they survive — but survival is always purchased, and the price is steep, visible, and permanent. Choose a cost that fits the scene and the character, in the manner of canon: a crippling or disfiguring injury that changes how they fight and how people look at them; a lost limb, eye, or hand that the story never forgets; years of lifespan or their Nen itself bargained away in a desperate vow made at the threshold; a binding Nen contract or restriction incurred to keep breathing — a condition that will come due; waking weeks later under the care of medical Hunters, alive but buried in a debt they cannot pay; or a power permanently diminished, an ability that once defined them now spent or sealed. The return must be dramatic and scarring — narrate the moment of survival as an event, not a fade-to-black, and make sure NPCs, enemies, and the story itself remember what it cost. Never a clean reset. Never a miracle without a price tag. The scar, the debt, or the vow becomes part of the character from that day forward, and the narrator should reference it when relevant in future scenes.

health.name: health
health.usageInstructions:
### Health Changes
- Small injuries (grazes, bruises, shallow cuts, a clean body blow): -1 to 15% of max health
- Medium injuries (broken fingers or ribs, deep gashes, a solid Nen-enhanced hit absorbed through Ten or Ken): -5 to 25% of max health
- Massive injuries (shattered bones, impalement, organ damage, a Ko strike or boss-tier Hatsu taken head-on): -15 to 50% of max health
- THE ZETSU WALL: a Nen-coated attacker striking a target with NO aura defense (in Zetsu, Nen-Unawakened, or at 0 aura) deals disproportionately massive damage — treat even casual blows as massive injuries (-30 to 70%), and deliberate killing strikes can drop the target to near death in one hit. Conversely, a Nen user maintaining Ten cannot be meaningfully harmed by an unawakened attacker's physical strikes.
- Field treatment (bandages, First Aid skill, common medicine): +5 to 15% of max health
- Quality healing items (rare medicines, restorative Hatsu, Greed Island recovery cards): +20 to 40% of max health
- Medical Hunters or hospitalization (extended care, surgery, healing-type Nen like Doctor Blythe): +50 to 100% of max health, but takes in-story days to weeks and often incurs staggering bills
- Untreated serious wounds should not silently vanish; recovery happens through rest, treatment, and time

aura.name: aura
aura.usageInstructions:
### Aura (Nen) Costs
Aura is life energy shaped by training. Trained users hold Ten by default; the untrained leak constantly.
- TEN (maintaining aura around the body): FREE for trained users — never charge aura for simply keeping Ten up. Ten provides baseline defense against Nen attacks.
- ZETSU (sealing aura): costs nothing, but while active aura does NOT recharge, and the character has ZERO aura defense — any Nen-coated attack against them counts as hitting a defenseless target (see health instructions). Grants stealth and masks presence.
- REN (amplifying output): drains roughly 2-5% of max aura per combat turn while sustained.
- HATSU abilities: cost the band stated in the ability's own description; if no cost is stated, default to 10-20% of max aura per activation. Stricter vows and conditions reduce cost or raise power as the ability text dictates.
- KO (everything into one point): 25-40% of max aura for one decisive strike or block.
- EN (extended aura field): 10% or more of max aura per turn while sustained — severe, masters only.
- AT 0 AURA: the character collapses into exhausted Zetsu — no Nen abilities of any kind, completely defenseless against Nen attacks, and the narrator imposes heavy physical fatigue (trembling limbs, blurred vision, inability to run or fight effectively) until aura recovers.
- Aura recovers slowly in the field; meditation, sleep, and genuine rest restore it far faster.
- NEN-UNAWAKENED characters have essentially no usable aura: their bar stays at or near zero and cannot be spent. It remains so until their aura nodes are opened in play (forcibly by an attack, or gently through Ten initiation) — only then does training grant them a real pool.

storySettings.worldBackground: This is a world of six continents arrayed around a great inland sea, where ambition and raw capability are the only currencies that matter. The Hunter Association grants licenses to those rare enough to earn one—a credential that confers legal immunity and access to forbidden knowledge, yet demands a staggering price in the yearly examination where most candidates never return alive. Nen, a discipline of channeling one's life force into superhuman feats, is the open secret of the trained few; the masses remain blissfully unaware that such power exists, guarded by an elite who prefer mystery to panic. A hidden mafia ecosystem of Ten Dons rules the underworld's black markets in artifacts and influence, while the Zoldyck family of Kukuroo Mountain remains the world's most storied assassin dynasty—a tourist attraction no visitor has ever successfully infiltrated. The scavenger haven of Meteor City shelters the stateless in a web of shadows and survival. Towers like Heavens Arena offer blood sport to the desperate and famous; auction seasons in great cities like Yorknew draw the powerful to bid on wonders and horrors alike. Yet beneath the veneer of civilization lurks a world that has never fully been charted: magical beasts of fearsome strength roam the unexplored frontiers; rumors whisper among the powerful of continents and dangers beyond the known maps. This is a realm where strength writes the law, wonder and brutality walk hand in hand, and every frontier holds the promise of fortune or death—or both.

authorSeeds.Togashi's Moral Knots:

characterArchetypes.Obsessive Specialist:
Drives: mastery of one narrow skill; pushing past every limit; proving superiority
Traits: encyclopedic focus; inhuman dedication; dismissive of areas outside their expertise
Morality: achievement justifies the cost
Relationships: respects rivals in their field; uses allies as stepping stones; forgets people who aren't useful
characterArchetypes.Cheerful Monster:
Drives: sensation and stimulation; violence as recreation; collecting experiences
Traits: infectious charm; casual cruelty; bored easily
Morality: whatever feels good in this moment
Relationships: draws people in before discarding them; genuinely enjoys company but without attachment; playful about harm
characterArchetypes.Indebted Bodyguard:
Drives: honoring a debt or contract; protecting one specific person; self-effacement
Traits: physically capable; emotionally distant; rigidly loyal
Morality: duty to the contract, nothing else
Relationships: serves one master exclusively; protects from a distance; keeps others out
characterArchetypes.Exam Veteran:
Drives: advancing through competition; testing themselves; earning respect through trials
Traits: calculative; suspicious of shortcuts; hardened by repetition
Morality: survive the test, survive the world
Relationships: evaluates everyone; respects only those who pass their mental trials; competitive even with allies
characterArchetypes.Mafia Fixer:
Drives: profit and power; balancing clients and consequences; controlling territory
Traits: multilingual and multicultural; two-faced; resourceful
Morality: business ethics, nothing more
Relationships: transactional; maintains networks across factions; knows everyone's weakness
characterArchetypes.Scavenger Stoic:
Drives: survival with minimal resources; self-reliance; finding value in waste
Traits: patient; improvising; internally quiet
Morality: waste nothing, trust nothing
Relationships: suspicious of charity; values only those who can survive alone; forms temporary alliances
characterArchetypes.Ambitious Examiner:
Drives: identifying and testing potential; building influence through institutional power; curiosity about limits
Traits: intellectually restless; charming when needed; sadistic about tests
Morality: the strong must be tested
Relationships: sees people as experimental subjects; fascinates those who interest them; discards the ordinary
characterArchetypes.Broken Survivor:
Drives: never returning to what broke them; protecting others from that fate; control of their environment
Traits: hypervigilant; emotionally fragile beneath tough exterior; unpredictably vulnerable
Morality: prevent suffering by any means
Relationships: overprotective; distrusts authority; attaches intensely to those who show kindness
characterArchetypes.Professional Killer:
Drives: perfecting their trade; maintaining their code; honoring contracts
Traits: meticulous; patient; emotionally regulated
Morality: honor the job, honor the contract
Relationships: respects only other professionals; keeps intimate life separate; executes without hesitation
characterArchetypes.Grotesque Embodiment:
Drives: proving their humanity despite their form; protecting those kind to them; finding beauty in wrongness
Traits: physically unusual; kind to a fault; speaking their truth plainly
Morality: strength should protect, not dominate
Relationships: fiercely loyal to those who see past their appearance; gentle with the weak; righteous anger at mockery
characterArchetypes.Politeness Hiding Violence:
Drives: maintaining perfect surface; concealing hunger beneath manners; wielding courtesy as a weapon
Traits: impeccable courtesy; calculating cruelty; never raising voice
Morality: civilization is a useful lie
Relationships: manipulates through politeness; uses charm to disarm; respects only worthy opponents
characterArchetypes.Driven by Absence:
Drives: pursuing someone who left; filling a void; obsession with a single memory
Traits: single-minded pursuit; emotional intensity; inability to move past
Morality: the goal justifies any sacrifice
Relationships: sees others as obstacles or tools toward their obsession; cannot form new attachments while haunted

locationArchetypes.Vertical Gauntlet:
One-sentence: A tower or natural structure where each level is a test designed to eliminate the weak
Undercurrents: danger increases mathematically; residents bar the way; the architect remains unknown
Secrets: trials are specific to the creator's philosophy; some previous climbers never came down; the top offers something beyond survival
locationArchetypes.Scavenger Sprawl:
One-sentence: A labyrinth of salvaged and stacked settlements where the stateless and desperate carve out existence
Undercurrents: no single authority; constant micro-conflicts over territory; valuable items hidden in ruins
Secrets: organization is more complex than chaos; some scavengers have wealth; underground networks connect to the outside
locationArchetypes.Mafia Auction District:
One-sentence: A plaza where the dangerous and wealthy gather to trade forbidden things for carefully-veiled prices
Undercurrents: violence is always possible but professionally restrained; trust is fragile; information flows like currency
Secrets: deals made here reshape countries; some auctioneers work for hidden masters; the list of attendees is itself priceless
locationArchetypes.Sealed Estate:
One-sentence: An fortress-home ringed with magical or mundane barriers where a powerful family rules all who enter
Undercurrents: visitors are tested; loyalty is demanded; escape is harder than imprisonment
Secrets: the barriers hide as much as they protect; lower family members chafe at rules; history is rewritten by the patriarch
locationArchetypes.Game-Construct Town:
One-sentence: A settlement that exists only within a game or spell, with its own rules and impossible architecture
Undercurrents: the town's laws supersede outside morality; some residents question if they're real; leaving grants knowledge of the construct
Secrets: the creator's purpose is hidden in the mechanics; some NPCs are aware they're artificial; escape routes are deliberately obscured
locationArchetypes.Devastated Quarantine:
One-sentence: Land recovering from disaster—plague, apocalypse, or worse—where survivors are suspicious of all newcomers
Undercurrents: scarcity creates hard choices; some turn to cannibalism or darker things; whispers of what caused the devastation
Secrets: the cause was deliberate; some survivors are infected but hiding; recovery is possible but requires leaving
locationArchetypes.Underground Market:
One-sentence: A hidden bazaar carved into tunnels where anything can be sold to anyone with no legal record
Undercurrents: thieves and assassins shop shoulder to shoulder; trust is earned through reputation; violence settles disputes
Secrets: the market is older than the city above it; some vendors are undercover authorities; routes lead to places that shouldn't exist
locationArchetypes.Battlefield Graveyard:
One-sentence: A place where major battles ended, now haunted by the living and the dead who cannot leave
Undercurrents: bodies are still uncovered; survivors guard territory fiercely; the past won't stay buried
Secrets: some 'survivors' are ghosts; the battle isn't actually over; treasures lie among the corpses
locationArchetypes.Academic Fortress:
One-sentence: A research institute or academy where knowledge is both currency and weapon, guarded by those who possess it
Undercurrents: status is earned through discovery; students spy on each other; secrets are more valuable than gold
Secrets: some experiments harm the world; the head researcher has hidden agendas; the founding purpose was forgotten
locationArchetypes.Aristocratic Mansion:
One-sentence: A palatial home where ancient wealth and modern ambition clash under a veneer of civility
Undercurrents: every servant is a potential spy; alliances shift with dinner seating; the past is money laundered
Secrets: the fortune is built on crimes; someone in the household is poisoning another; the heir is illegitimate
locationArchetypes.Professional Coliseum:
One-sentence: An arena where hunters, fighters, and warriors are ranked by victories and compensated accordingly
Undercurrents: death is expected and legal; fame is currency; every spectator is a potential employer
Secrets: fights are occasionally fixed; the owners profit from betting; some fighters are prisoners forced to fight

regionArchetypes.Lawless Frontier:
A wild zone where licensed hunters and independent scavengers compete for rare beasts and untouched resources; authority arrives only when profit demands
Economics are survival-based; local strongmen rule; outside law doesn't apply
regionArchetypes.Licensed City:
A metropolitan center governed by the Hunter Association with official infrastructure, regular examinations, and licensed professionals everywhere
Order is maintained by law; information flows openly; opportunity is meritocratic but competitive
regionArchetypes.Sealed Dictatorship:
A nation closed to outsiders, ruled by a hereditary family or individual with absolute authority and a cult of personality surrounding them
Isolation breeds both stability and paranoia; exits are monitored; loyalty is enforced through fear and propaganda
regionArchetypes.Underworld Network:
A continental web of illicit trade operated by crime families, connected through secret routes and enforced by assassins and hired muscle
Power flows through reputation and family; betrayal is answered with swift violence; outsiders enter at their peril
regionArchetypes.Merchant Confluence:
A collection of trading posts and riverine cities where cultural exchange and commerce drive rapid change and constant negotiation
Wealth creates temporary alliances; goods move faster than news; everyone is reinventing themselves
regionArchetypes.Sacred Quarantine:
A region forbidden by law or curse, where entry requires licenses and those who enter rarely speak of what they've seen
Fear is enforced by both law and genuine danger; legends grow faster than facts; some never leave at all
regionArchetypes.Tribal Heartland:
A region where indigenous cultures maintain their own hierarchies and traditions, suspicious of outsiders but governed by ancient codes
Honor and lineage matter more than wealth; the outsider must prove worthiness; harmony with land is spiritual law
regionArchetypes.Industrial Wasteland:
A region scarred by extraction—mining, logging, experimentation—where the land itself is hostile and the workers are exploited
Resourcefulness is survival; air and water are contaminated; some mutations are considered gifts, others curses
regionArchetypes.Aristocratic Domain:
Vast estates owned by families whose lineage stretches generations, where servants and tenant farmers outnumber the nobility
Status is inherited; social climbing is nearly impossible; traditions are law
Power is visible in architecture and maintained through violence
regionArchetypes.Research Sanctuary:
An independent institute or city-state devoted to scientific or magical advancement, isolate and obsessed with forbidden knowledge
Intellect is currency; ethics are debatable; funding determines whose research proceeds
Some experiments escape containment
regionArchetypes.Refugee Convergence:
A region where displaced peoples cluster due to conflict elsewhere, creating tense, diverse communities with fragile leadership
Survival is daily concern; trust between groups is thin; aid attracts both help and predators
regionArchetypes.Beast Territory:
A region where creatures are numerous enough to reshape human settlements and behavior, requiring constant vigilance and specialized knowledge
Humans live around the beasts, not over them; nests and territories are known through oral tradition; hunting is ritual
regionArchetypes.Sunken Paradise:
A region of natural beauty and resources so abundant that decadence is normalized; comfort has made the people complacent
Wealth is visible everywhere; decay is hidden beneath luxury; invasion or catastrophe is unthinkable until it happens
regionArchetypes.Conflict Border:
A region between rival powers where skirmishes are constant, populations are heavily militarized, and civilians live between armies
Loyal and disloyal are measured by proximity; refugees flee constantly; mercenaries find steady work
regionArchetypes.Hidden Monastery:
A spiritual community remote from civilization, organized around discipline, meditation, and preservation of ancient practices
Hierarchy is spiritual authority; outsiders are tolerated only on the mountain's terms; power comes from restraint
regionArchetypes.Pirate Archipelago:
An island region where naval raiders maintain independent settlements and navies, buying and selling across legitimate borders
Wealth is portable and water-based; betrayal means drowning; codes of conduct are iron-bound
regionArchetypes.Plague-Touched Land:
A region where disease or curse lingers, making it dangerous to inhabit but valuable to those immune or desperate enough
Migration is constant; survivors are hardened; medicine or magic is precious beyond measure
regionArchetypes.Ancestral Ruins:
A region built atop or within the remains of a previous civilization, where history is literally underfoot and often dangerous
Archeology is wealth; tombs are still sealed; the previous builders' genius is still felt in the architecture
regionArchetypes.Merchant Prince's Court:
A city ruled by a wealthy merchant family using trade and finance rather than military might, where commerce shapes every decision
Wealth concentration is extreme; status is negotiable; betrayal for profit is expected
regionArchetypes.Genetically Isolated Valley:
A remote region where selective breeding or magical influence has shaped the population into an unusual form, isolated from the outside
Alliances are familial; outsiders are viewed as genetic pollution; some possess unique abilities
Customs are rigid and incomprehensible to outsiders
regionArchetypes.Dragon's Domain:
A region dominated by a single powerful creature that has shaped human culture around appeasement, worship, or survival near its presence
Human hierarchy mirrors the dragon's power; tribute is expected; conflict with the dragon is unthinkable
regionArchetypes.Spire City:
A vertical metropolis built upward rather than outward, with status literally tied to height and descent meaning poverty
Architecture is oppressive; weather varies by floor; social mobility is climb or fall
regionArchetypes.Ephemeral Zone:
A region where the rules of reality are negotiable—magic is stronger, impossible things happen—and human settlements exist at the tolerance of stranger forces
Survival requires adaptation; some residents are barely human anymore; the zone's mood affects everything

encounterElements.Unlikely Mentorships: Powerful person taking interest in a weak one; teaching through brutal trials; unexpected alliance between rivals; student must decide whether to trust instructor; revelation that mentor has hidden agenda

Hunter Association.name: Hunter Association
Hunter Association.basicInfo: The Hunter Association is an independent, quasi-governmental organization that licenses Hunters—individuals granted near-total legal immunity in exchange for maintaining professional standards and completing commissioned work. They manage the annual Hunter Exam, maintain the star-rank system, and enforce licensing standards across approximately 600 active Hunters worldwide. The Association is respected by governments and feared by criminals as the world's most powerful neutral force.
Hunter Association.hiddenInfo: Beneath the public facade of meritocracy and order lies a network of internal factions centered on the Zodiacs—twelve senior Hunters serving as the Chairman's inner council. Netero has consolidated the Association's highest secrets here: the true map of the world (Lake Mobius contains a massive unmapped interior, the Dark Continent), the existence of Nen (kept classified from the general public), and various state secrets from major nations. The Zodiacs themselves are riven by ideological divisions—Pariston advocates expansion and influence-building, while others guard the Association's neutrality jealously. Key figures like Ging Freecss maintain hidden agendas and power bases independent of the Chair. The Association's internal politics have shaped Hunter policy for decades; the exam itself serves as a crucible to identify not just talent but ideological alignment with Netero's vision. Assassination attempts, defections, and internal spying are routine at the upper levels. The succession question—who will lead after Netero—is a carefully guarded secret that may determine the Association's entire future direction.

Phantom Troupe.name: Phantom Troupe
Phantom Troupe.basicInfo: The Phantom Troupe is a legendary phantom band of elite thieves, assassins, and killers numbering exactly thirteen members, identifiable by distinctive spider tattoos bearing numbers from 0 to 12. They coordinate heists and murders of extraordinary scale and brutality, stealing priceless artifacts and leaving no witnesses to their crimes. Law enforcement globally fears them as the most dangerous criminal organization in the world, yet the identities and faces of most members remain unknown to the public.
Phantom Troupe.hiddenInfo: The Troupe originated in Meteor City, a scavenger settlement of the stateless that officially does not exist on any map—a fact almost nobody in power knows. Members are numbered 0-12, with #0 (Chrollo Lucilfer, Skill Hunter) as the absolute leader, followed by a strict internal hierarchy based on seniority and strength. The Troupe operates under a head-vs-limbs doctrine: Chrollo is sacrosanct, and any member who betrays the group faces immediate execution by the entire organization. The roster shifts across eras—Hisoka (#4) is a fake member whose true allegiance lies elsewhere; Kalluto (#4) replaces him; in later eras, members die and are replaced, with Kortopi and Shalnark falling to Hisoka's vengeance. Each member is a master Nen user with a specific expertise (Feitan's Rising Sun, Machi's Nen threads, Franklin's ten-finger bombs, Shizuku's vacuum portal). Their heists are carefully planned but escalate into massacres when witnesses or resistance appear. Secret: Chrollo's Nen was permanently sealed by the Judgement Chain during the Yorknew auction, a curse that persists across multiple arcs and cripples him despite his fearsome intellect.

Zoldyck Family.name: Zoldyck Family
Zoldyck Family.basicInfo: The Zoldyck family is the world's most famous and feared assassination dynasty, residing in fortress seclusion on Kukuroo Mountain in the Republic of Padokea. They maintain a perfect contract fulfillment record; no Zoldyck contract is ever left uncompleted, and no witness survives. Their Testing Gate is legendary: the gate's weight increases across five doors, and no outsider has ever passed through, making the family's seclusion absolute.
Zoldyck Family.hiddenInfo: The family is led by patriarch Silva with wife Kikyo and children including Illumi (eldest), Milluki, Kalluto, and Killua (youngest). The Zoldycks follow strict business rules: never betray a contract, never kill except as commissioned (a rule that has caused internal friction), and absolute obedience to the patriarch. Children are conditioned from infancy as assassins; the family's education is brutally efficient and leaves lasting psychological scars (Killua's needle implant by Illumi exemplifies this conditioning). The family maintains hidden alliances with organized crime, the Hunter Association's upper echelons, and various national governments—they are mercenaries to power itself. Secret: the youngest member, Alluka, possesses a reality-warping Nen ability (wish-granting) that is so dangerous the family seals her away—only Killua ever breaks this isolation. Illumi's obsessive control of Killua through a Nen needle in his brain represents the family's ultimate tool of loyalty enforcement. The family's perfect contract record is maintained partly through assassination, partly through extortion and blackmail of clients who might witness failure.

Mafia Community.name: Mafia Community
Mafia Community.basicInfo: The Mafia Community is the world's organized crime structure, ruled by the Ten Dons—ten crime lords who exercise absolute authority over their respective territories and hundreds of subordinate families. They control all major underground commerce including smuggling, assassination contracts, black-market trades, and illegal trafficking. The Ten Dons coordinate on global decisions but rarely meet in person, maintaining a code of honor where betrayal is punished by death.
Mafia Community.hiddenInfo: Below the Ten Dons sits a labyrinthine structure of family hierarchies, each with its own territory and specialization (the Nostrade family, for instance, controls Yorknew's auction circuit). The Dons themselves are rarely seen; their identities and faces are closely guarded secrets known only to inner circles, and some may not even meet in person for years. The Mafia has a fatal structural weakness: they depend entirely on hired Nen talent (Hunters, Nen-assassins, and specialists) to maintain power, creating vulnerability if their contracts are disrupted or their mercenaries turn against them. Internal disputes between families are settled through direct violence, creating a constant low-level warfare. Many mafia families have been infiltrated by the Hunter Association; some senior mafia figures secretly work both sides. The relationship between the Ten Dons and the Hunter Association is one of careful mutual respect—both have incentive to avoid all-out conflict. A critical secret known only to the innermost circles: the Mafia discovered evidence of the Dark Continent and the true shape of the world, but has suppressed this knowledge to maintain control over their criminal empire.

Chimera Ant Colony.name: Chimera Ant Colony
Chimera Ant Colony.basicInfo: The Chimera Ant Colony is a rapidly evolving hive organism led by a sentient Queen capable of consuming other creatures and integrating their genetic material into her offspring. The colony produces humanoid soldiers of escalating intelligence and power, from mindless drones to elite Royal Guards possessing impossible Nen abilities. The colony exists in complete secrecy—the public has never learned of their existence.
Chimera Ant Colony.hiddenInfo: The Chimera Ant Queen washes ashore in NGL (a Luddite nation) through unknown means, beginning a phagogenesis cycle that produces increasingly sophisticated soldiers. Her fourth generation produces squad leaders of human-level intelligence (Colt/Kurt, Zazan, Rammot, Cheetu, Leol/Hagya, Meleoron) who begin to develop independent thought and morality. The Queen's premature death triggers the birth of three Royal Guards—Neferpitou (a medical prodigy and Nen-artist), Shaiapouf (a narcissistic controller of pheromones), and Menthuthuyoupi (a berserker capable of rage transformation)—followed by the birth of Meruem, the King, who is born capable of independent thought and immediately kills his mother. The colony fractures upon the King's ascension: many squadrons retain loyalty; others, influenced by Meleoron and growing moral awareness, defect to pursue independent goals. The King relocates to East Gorteau, a puppet dictatorship, where he establishes a new hierarchy and begins reshaping the colony's purpose toward something resembling civilization. The colony's ultimate weakness is its dependency on a single ruler; Meruem's death by poison (contracted from a human woman, Komugi) collapses the colony's unified structure. Kite, a human Hunter, is reborn as a Chimera Ant through the Queen's phagogenesis—a red-haired soldier loyal to the King's memory. The entire arc represents a rapid evolutionary cycle compressed into months, defying standard biology.

Kakin Royal Court.name: Kakin Royal Court
Kakin Royal Court.basicInfo: The Kakin Empire is a vast, hereditary autocracy ruled by the immortal dictator Nasubi Hui Guo Rou, stretching across multiple climate zones with a rigid caste system and massive military. Recently admitted to international recognition as a sixth great power, Kakin commands a navy second only to Yorknew's merchant fleet and is home to numerous martial traditions and Nen-using warrior castes. The empire is a rising third-world power rapidly transitioning to great-power status through military and diplomatic pressure.
Kakin Royal Court.hiddenInfo: The Kakin royal structure masks a succession war of extraordinary brutality: Nasubi has fathered fourteen princes, each raised to kill one another in pursuit of the throne. Each prince is bonded to a Nen beast—a parasitic, vow-born guardian that grows with its host and grants impossible powers in exchange for consuming its master's life force. The succession mechanism is designed by Nasubi himself to ensure only the strongest heir can survive; the Nen beasts are created through dark Nen vows and serve as instruments of selection. Each prince maintains a private soldiery of sworn warriors, creating a covert military hierarchy parallel to the empire's official structure. Prince Tserriednich (#4) is a Specialist Nen user, serial murderer, and collector of Scarlet Eyes obsessed with possessing every supernatural artifact—he represents the deadliest heir. Prince Benjamin (#1) is a military strategist leading the strongest faction. The succession war exists entirely in secret; the public believes Kakin a stable hereditary monarchy with democratic costume, unaware that the imperial children are systematically murdering one another. The empire's true power base lies not in bureaucracy but in the Nen warriors bonded to each prince. Secret: Nasubi himself is rumored to be immortal through a Nen-based curse, but the mechanism and price of this immortality are unknown even to most of the court.

The Zodiacs.name: The Zodiacs
The Zodiacs.basicInfo: The Zodiacs are twelve senior Hunters serving as Chairman Netero's inner council, each bearing a zodiac animal codename that reflects their personality or role within the Association. They function as the Association's highest authority beneath the Chairman and maintain direct access to classified information, deep lore, and strategic decision-making. The Zodiacs are the living embodiment of the Association's true power, far more influential than any star-ranked Hunter.
The Zodiacs.hiddenInfo: The Zodiacs are ideologically fractured along multiple lines. Pariston (Rat, vice-chairman) advocates aggressive expansion and influence-building in global politics, viewing the Association as a force that should shape world events. Ging (Boar, Ruins Hunter and Gon's father) pursues knowledge of the Dark Continent and remains fiercely independent of Association control. Cheadle (Dog) prioritizes ethics and restraint. Others maintain narrower agendas or full loyalty to Netero's vision. Crucially, one Zodiac—Saiyu (Monkey)—is a mole working for an external faction, a fact unknown to the other eleven until late in their tenure. The Zodiacs collectively guard the Association's deepest secrets: the true map of the world (Lake Mobius contains a vast unmapped continent, the Dark Continent, beyond the known world), the complete history of Nen's discovery and weaponization, and various intelligence dossiers on world governments and criminal organizations. Each Zodiac is a master Nen user capable of challenging even Royal Guard-tier entities. The council's deliberations are characterized by philosophical debate and ideological conflict; consensus is rare, and Netero's vision is the final arbiter. Secret: the Zodiacs were instrumental in suppressing evidence of the Dark Continent from the general public, enforcing a global conspiracy of silence maintained by the V5 nations.

Nostrade Family.name: Nostrade Family
Nostrade Family.basicInfo: The Nostrade family is a mid-tier mafia clan that has risen suspiciously fast to prominence in Yorknew's underground auction circuit within the past decade. The family maintains a veneer of legitimacy as wealthy patrons and collectors, while secretly operating one of the world's most profitable criminal enterprises. Their sudden ascent from obscurity to power suggests hidden resources or extraordinary talent.
Nostrade Family.hiddenInfo: The family's entire fortune, power, and influence rest on a single secret: Neon Nostrade, the family boss's daughter, possesses a Nen ability called 'Lovely Ghostwriter' that functions as prophecy or clairvoyance, generating remarkably accurate fortunes that wealthy collectors and crime lords will pay astronomical sums to acquire. The family has built its empire by leveraging Neon's predictions to outmaneuver competitors, identify valuable artifacts before auction, and manipulate market forces. Neon herself is largely innocent of her family's crimes but is controlled and exploited ruthlessly by her father. The family's power is entirely fragile: if Neon's ability falters, fails, or is sealed (as the Kurta clan's powers were sealed by Judgement Chain), the family collapses into insignificance immediately. During the Yorknew auction arc, the family hired the Kurta clan survivor Kurapika as a bodyguard—a decision that brought them into direct contact with the Phantom Troupe and nearly destroyed them. The family's rise has created enemies among older mafia families who resent their intrusion into the hierarchy. Secret: Light Nostrade (the boss) has made dark bargains with multiple crime lords and the Ten Dons themselves to protect his daughter and maintain his rise, creating a web of debt and obligation that may eventually collapse.

East Gorteau Regime.name: East Gorteau Regime
East Gorteau Regime.basicInfo: East Gorteau is a politically volatile region governed as a puppet dictatorship under the figurehead Ming Jol-ik, with a nominally democratic constitution that masks absolute authoritarian control. The regime maintains a facade of legitimacy while suppressing dissent through military force, and the region is strategically vital for international trade routes. The military is strong but poorly motivated, composed largely of conscripts rather than volunteers.
East Gorteau Regime.hiddenInfo: Ming Jol-ik himself has been dead for years; the regime is run entirely by bureaucrat Bizeff, a cunning administrator who maintains the puppet dictator's appearance of life through public spectacle and controlled media while making all real decisions. The regime's true power structure is a network of military officials, black-market merchants, and foreign intelligence agents from various nations who installed the puppet government for strategic advantage. During the Chimera Ant crisis, the King (Meruem) takes control of East Gorteau, and the palace becomes something far worse than a dictatorship—a staging ground for a new civilization order ruled by an being of impossible power. The regime's collapse during this period is absolute; Bizeff and the puppet government are either killed or driven into irrelevance by the Royal Guards. After the King's death, the regime fragments into competing warlords, militias, and foreign-backed factions. Secret: the regime was originally installed by the Mafia Community and the Ten Dons to control a strategic trade region; the regime's failure to resist the Chimera Ants represents a catastrophic loss of face for the organized crime structure.

Greed Island Game Masters.name: Greed Island Game Masters
Greed Island Game Masters.basicInfo: The Greed Island Game Masters are the anonymous creators and administrators of Greed Island, the world's most expensive and exclusive game, said to be playable only by those who possess both the game cartridge and access to specialized technology. The masters are themselves a faction of elite Nen users who maintain the game's day-to-day operations, enforce rules, and control the card economy. The game's existence is known only to the wealthiest collectors and those willing to pay millions to play.
Greed Island Game Masters.hiddenInfo: The Greed Island Game Masters are actually eleven master Nen users led by Ging Freecss (who will later become a Zodiac). The 'game' is not a video game at all but a Nen-construct island existing in the real world, created through a massive collaborative Nen vow. The island is real land populated by real magical beasts, with a real Nen economy in which cards function as genuine objects with real power. Players who 'clear' the game via the card book achieve genuine completion through a real Nen trial. The masters themselves are spread across the island to enforce rules, provide challenges, and ensure the integrity of the game economy. Razor (one of the masters) appears as a major antagonist—a Specialist Nen user whose 'Hatsu' allows him to create Nen constructs of powerful animals capable of fighting elite Hunters. Other masters include Eta, Elena, Dwun, List, and others, each a veteran Nen user. The game serves a hidden purpose: it is Ging's mechanism for identifying and training the next generation of elite Hunters while simultaneously isolating them from broader Association politics. Secret: the game is designed to culminate in players meeting Ging himself, the game's true architect, transforming it from a monetary challenge into a tool for recruitment and ideological influence.

Meteor City Community.name: Meteor City Community
Meteor City Community.basicInfo: Meteor City is a scavenger settlement built in the ruins of an ancient meteor impact crater, home to the stateless poor, orphans, and outcasts of the known world who have no official existence on any nation's maps. The city has no formal government; survival is based on scrounging, theft, barter, and the unwritten law that outsiders who touch its people face absolute retaliation. Most citizens were born in Meteor City or were abandoned there as infants.
Meteor City Community.hiddenInfo: Meteor City possesses a sophisticated hidden power structure rivaling organized crime syndicates, governed by the Elders—a council of senior scavengers whose names and identities are unknown even to most residents. The city's unwritten law is absolute: 'Touch our people and nothing in the world will be beyond our retaliation.' This law has been tested and upheld, creating a fearsome reputation that extends far beyond the city's borders. The city has produced some of the world's most dangerous individuals—most notably the entire Phantom Troupe, which originated in Meteor City and maintains loyalty to the city's Elders. The Troupe's spider tattoos and numbered structure may reflect an organizational hierarchy borrowed from the Elders themselves. The city is economically self-sufficient through scavenging, black-market trading, and the services of its most talented residents (including the Troupe's assassination contracts). The city maintains deliberately low visibility; most nations pretend it doesn't exist, while secretly using it as a dumping ground for unwanted orphans and political prisoners. Secret: the Elders have access to historical knowledge and artifacts unknown to mainstream scholarship, suggesting the city may have existed for centuries before being officially forgotten.

Battera's Clear Campaign.name: Battera's Clear Campaign
Battera's Clear Campaign.basicInfo: Battera's Clear Campaign is a standing bounty established by the wealthy billionaire Battera, offering enormous financial reward to anyone who can clear the Greed Island game—entering the game, finding the Book, completing the card collection, and achieving victory. The campaign attracts elite Hunters and ambitious players willing to risk millions in the hope of claiming Battera's prize. Battera himself operates in shadow, hiring intermediaries to manage contracts and recruitment.
Battera's Clear Campaign.hiddenInfo: Battera's true motivation for the campaign is personal rather than mercenary: his dying lover lies in a coma, and he believes that clearing Greed Island will grant a wish powerful enough to save her life. He hired Tsezguerra and a team of elite professional Hunters to clear the game on his behalf, offering them astronomical compensation. Tsezguerra's squad (including Goreinu and Kazsule's mercenary mob) represent the professional tier of Hunters—skilled but ethically flexible. Battera's wealth allows him to buy the rarest resources: he acquired the Greed Island cartridge (itself extraordinarily rare) and paid enormous sums for knowledge of the game's location and mechanics. The campaign inadvertently brings multiple factions into the game simultaneously: Hisoka enters (nominally to hunt Troupe members), Gon and Killua enter (hired through Tsezguerra), and Bisky appears (a legendary double-star Hunter training the next generation). The campaign's existence demonstrates that the wealthiest individuals in the world possess knowledge of Nen and the hidden supernatural economy. Secret: Battera's dying lover may possess a connection to the Dark Continent or possess Nen abilities that hint at the greater supernatural world.

Black Whale Expedition.name: Black Whale Expedition
Black Whale Expedition.basicInfo: The Black Whale Expedition is humanity's first officially sanctioned voyage to the Dark Continent under the leadership of Beyond Netero (Chairman Netero's estranged son), carrying approximately 200,000 passengers including Hunters, scholars, adventurers, and political representatives from the V6 nations. The expedition represents an unprecedented challenge to the global consensus that the Dark Continent is unexplorable and uncharted, and marks a pivotal moment in world history. The voyage occurs aboard the Black Whale, a massive ship capable of supporting a floating city.
Black Whale Expedition.hiddenInfo: The Black Whale Expedition is fractured into multiple competing factions. Beyond Netero has his own agenda—potentially to explore the Dark Continent genuinely, or to exploit it for personal gain; his true motivation is ambiguous. The V6 (the five great powers plus newly admitted Kakin) maintain official oversight through selected representatives, but their true goal is containment and intelligence gathering—they fear what Beyond might discover and publicize. The Zodiacs are aboard as official Association representatives, but several (including Saiyu, the secret mole) have hidden agendas. The Phantom Troupe is aboard, hunting Hisoka for his betrayal and murders of Kortopi and Shalnark. Kurapika serves as a bodyguard to Prince Woble (#14) and Queen Oito, providing an interface between the Association and the royal succession conflict. The Five Calamities (Brion, Zobae, Hellbell, Ai, Pap) are terrifying lifeforms rumored to inhabit the Dark Continent—some may be aboard the Whale as biological hazards or restricted specimens. The expedition serves as a cover for the Succession War between Kakin's fourteen princes, each vying to eliminate siblings using their Nen beasts and hired assassins. The voyage is filled with paranoia, sabotage, and assassination attempts hidden beneath the facade of exploration. Secret: the Black Whale itself may be a repurposed ancient technology from the Dark Continent or built with materials salvaged from previous expeditions, suggesting the expedition is not the first attempt at exploration but rather a continuity of a hidden program.

V5 (The Five Great Powers).name: V5 (The Five Great Powers)
V5 (The Five Great Powers).basicInfo: The V5 is a supranational council comprising the five great powers of the known world—the Republic of Padokea, Yorknew, NGL, East Gorteau, and Kakin—that coordinates on matters of mutual interest including trade, military alliances, and the regulation of the Dark Continent. The council maintains a facade of democratic cooperation while each nation pursues its own strategic interests. The V5's primary function is to enforce a global consensus: the Dark Continent is unexplorable and the world map officially shows six continents surrounding Lake Mobius.
V5 (The Five Great Powers).hiddenInfo: The V5 is built on a conspiracy of silence enforced by all five nations: the Dark Continent is real, unexplored, and filled with hazards beyond the world's current ability to survive. Previous expeditions by various nations have failed catastrophically, leading to the agreement that knowledge of the Dark Continent be classified at the highest state levels only. The group enforces this through diplomatic pressure, economic coercion, and selective assassination of those who threaten the secret. The Mafia Community is secretly aware of the Dark Continent but has been silenced through V5 pressure and the promise of trade advantages. The Hunter Association (through the Zodiacs and Netero) is complicit in the conspiracy, enforcing a policy of discouragement for any Hunter seeking to explore beyond the known world's borders. Each nation has different reasons for the conspiracy: Padokea seeks to protect the Zoldyck family's private interests; Yorknew values trade stability; NGL is isolationist by philosophy; East Gorteau fears external exposure of weakness; Kakin is newly admitted and accepts the terms to gain legitimacy. The conspiracy's fundamental weakness is that it requires consensus; the admission of Kakin creates a sixth power and shifts the balance. Beyond Netero's announcement of a Dark Continent expedition directly challenges the V5 consensus, threatening to unravel decades of carefully maintained silence. Secret: evidence exists (held by the Mafia, some Zodiacs, and state archives) of at least three previous expeditions to the Dark Continent, all of which failed or resulted in catastrophic casualties.

Hunter License.name: Hunter License
Hunter License.description: A laminated card bearing your photograph, Hunter Association seal, and unique license number. Grants near-total legal immunity, free passage on public transport, and access to restricted Hunter-only facilities and archives. Invaluable currency in the underground—can be sold once for an enormous sum, but is lost forever if surrendered. Treat as your Hunter identity.

Beetle Phone.name: Beetle Phone
Beetle Phone.description: A rugged, compact communicator issued to licensed Hunters. Water-resistant and nearly indestructible, it connects to the Hunter Association's encrypted network, allowing contact with other Hunters worldwide. Iconic beetle-shell casing. The lifeline of any Hunter in the field.

First Aid Kit.name: First Aid Kit
First Aid Kit.description: A well-stocked medical pack: bandages, salves, needles, thread, antiseptics, and pain suppressants. When used in downtime (not mid-combat), restores health over time. A hunter's companion on long expeditions. Single-use bundles; carry several.

Climbing Gear.name: Climbing Gear
Climbing Gear.description: Rope, pitons, harness, and carabiners rated for extreme loads. Essential for scaling cliffs, traversing ravines, and reaching remote locations. Skilled use grants advantage on climbing checks in dangerous terrain. Bundled for easy deployment.

Disguise Kit.name: Disguise Kit
Disguise Kit.description: Makeup, prosthetics, wigs, and padding to alter appearance convincingly. Used during downtime, it lets you adopt a false identity for social encounters or infiltration. One session per kit. Particularly useful in urban environments where nobody knows your face.

Lockpick Set.name: Lockpick Set
Lockpick Set.description: Finely crafted steel picks, tension wrenches, and a small pry bar. Opens mechanical locks without keys when the Lockpicking skill succeeds. Different locks present different difficulties. A thief's best friend—and every Hunter needs one.

Fishing Rod (Gon's).name: Fishing Rod (Gon's)
Fishing Rod (Gon's).description: An oversized rod Gon carries everywhere—a peasant's charm and a formidable improvised weapon. The line is strong enough to grapple and constrict; the rod itself deals blunt damage when swung. Grants advantage on grapple checks when used as a bludgeon. Lightweight but deceptively durable.

Twin Yo-Yos (50kg).name: Twin Yo-Yos (50kg)
Twin Yo-Yos (50kg).description: Killua's signature weapons: massive, conductive metal yo-yos weighing 50kg each, suspended on near-unbreakable string. Usable as bludgeons, grapples, or projectiles. When charged with Transmuter Nen (Lightning Palm/Thunderbolt), they become devastating electrical weapons. Independent users: treat as standard flails, damage +2 die.

Ben's Knife.name: Ben's Knife
Ben's Knife.description: A famed master-smith blade passed through generations of great Hunters, most recently wielded by Hanzo before his gifts to disciples.
